opening.headline: When copying chat responses and transferring them to documents is repeated, you will learn how to determine the unit of results by creating artifacts and files.
body: When a well-organized answer comes out of the chat, copy the content, move it to a document, slide, or table, and reformat it. If you request a correction, a new answer will appear and you will have to move it again. Since the results are only in the chat, it is difficult to use them for a long time or show them to others.

Claude has two ways to reduce this problem: Artifacts can be opened next to a conversation to be edited and shared, and file creation allows you to run code to instantly create Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and PDF files. In this class, we will identify what the two functions are and explain the criteria for determining whether a conversation is sufficient or an output is necessary, using examples of web page drafts and reports.
objectives: Can explain the role of artifacts and file creation functions
You can distinguish whether the result is a conversation or a product.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

screens.title: Copying the answer and transferring it to a document
screens.lead: Find out what happens when you move chat results into work documents. When you select each item, an explanation will unfold.

items.prompt: There was a well-organized answer in the chat.
items.answer: This is a good situation where the structure and content that fit the needs were created all at once. The problem is that these results are inside the chat window.

items.prompt: Translate the answer into a document, slide, or table.
items.answer: Copy and paste your answers into a text editor or spreadsheet, re-adjusting the font, table appearance, and item numbers. The content is already there, but it takes time to move and decorate it.

items.prompt: What happens if I request a correction?
items.answer: If you ask to correct a sentence, a new answer will appear, and it will not be reflected in the document you have already moved. You have to move the new answer again or go back and forth between the two places to fix it.

The problem is that the results are only in the chat, so it is difficult to open them again, edit them, show them to others, or write them into a file. You can reduce this repetition by changing the unit of output to artifacts rather than conversations.

screens.outro: First, let's think about the time it takes to move it.

screens.title: Think about it: how long it takes to move
screens.lead: Read the questions and think for yourself first. There is no need to submit an answer, and when you select an item, the instructor's thoughts unfold.

items.prompt: How much time do you spend translating chat results into documents or tables?
items.answer: Sometimes it feels like it takes longer to move and format the content than to create it. If this time is repeated frequently, it is a sign that the form of the result may change.

items.prompt: Where can I make changes after moving?
items.answer: If you make changes only in the transferred document, it will be inconsistent with the contents of the chat, and if you make changes in the chat, it will be inconsistent with the document. It's easy to get confused about which version is the most recent.

items.prompt: Who sees the results and how often?
items.answer: The results that I read once and the results that many people review and revise over and over again require different forms. This difference becomes the judgment standard for this class. The more viewers and the more edits you make, the more inconvenient the results will be in the chat. Please keep this in mind.

screens.outro: Now let's take a look at what Artifacts are.

screens.title: Artifacts: Artifacts that open next to a conversation.
screens.lead: If you hover over or select an underlined term in the following article, an explanation will appear.

visual.alt: Claude screen mockup with output windows open next to the dialog window

data.text: Artifact is suitable output for design, slides, documents, dashboards, or small interactive tools that you can share with others. It can be opened alongside a conversation, allowing you to edit it directly or ask Claude to make changes, and you can return to it later to share again. You can start creating from a conversation, or from Docs, Slides, or Design (template). The generated outputs are collected in the sidebar's Artifacts tab, where you can find and revisit them. Artifacts can be created from chat plans ranging from Free to Enterprise, with some variations depending on your plan, such as the Dashboard (template). However, to use Artifacts, the cloud (Execute code and create files) must be enabled.

terms.tip: It is a result that the person who created it can show to others. Claude creates Artifacts when they are long, self-contained, and likely to be reworked or reused.
Starter forms such as Docs, Slides, Design, Dashboards (beta), and Motion (beta). Select it from Output in the message box or select it from the Artifacts tab.
The sidebar is where all the output I have created is displayed in one place. You can find and open it again from any conversation.

This feature can be turned on in Capabilities in Settings. Free, Pro, and Max are managed in settings, and Team and Enterprise are managed in organization settings. If it is turned off, Artifacts cannot be used.

screens.outro: Next, let's look at how file creation works.

screens.title: Create, edit and share files
screens.lead: In the following steps we will see how file creation is turned on and used. Select the next arrow to proceed.

steps.title: What is it?
steps.body: Claude runs code to create Excel spreadsheets, PowerPoint presentations, Word documents, and PDF files right in conversation. If you make a request in natural language, you can download the created file and use it right away. It can be used by all users on the web, desktop, and mobile.

steps.title: what can you make
steps.body: You can create financial models with working formulas in Excel, reports with charts and visuals, and presentations pulled from existing documents. Advanced analysis of uploaded data is also possible. The key is that you can create documents just by talking, even without specialized software skills.

steps.title: How to turn it on varies depending on the plan.
steps.body: For Free, Pro, and Max accounts, turn on Code execution and file creation in Capabilities in Settings. Team and Enterprise are turned on by default at the organization level and can be turned off by owners in their organization settings. You can also turn it on or off in Capabilities in Settings on mobile.

steps.title: network access
steps.body: To access external data, turn on Allow network egress. Free, Pro, and Max have network access turned on to install packages from approved sources. In Team and Enterprise, network access is turned off by default and turned on by owners in their organization settings. Enterprise also allows you to set up access controls, such as domain whitelists.

steps.title: Fix and Share
steps.body: The resulting work can be reopened and modified later. Artifacts can be edited by talking to Claude or edited directly if created as a template, and in documents, if you select the text to be edited and request Edit with Claude, only the marked areas will be edited. Once completed, export or share with Export to Word, PDF, Markdown, Google Docs, PowerPoint, etc.

screens.outro: Now that we've seen the two features, let's summarize the criteria that distinguish dialogue from output.

screens.title: Distinguish between conversations and deliverables
screens.lead: Switch between the two states and compare the dialogue answers and output to see which situation is appropriate.

states.label: conversation answer
states.body: Conversational responses are great for quick explanations, quick confirmations, or listing ideas. There is no need to create separate content that will end its role after reading. If you turn all your answers into outputs, you actually have more things to manage. Short answers to short questions are best left in the chat. For example, it is natural to end a conversation by asking about the meaning of a term or refining a sentence, and if you need to reuse the results later, it is not too late to transfer them to the output at that time.

states.label: output
states.body: The output is suitable for results that need to be reopened, modified, shown to others, and written to a file. Claude creates Artifacts when the content is long and self-contained, has a high potential for editing or reuse, and is intended to be referenced again later. The longer the result is used, the more important the format is, and the more it is shared, the better the result becomes and the less effort it takes to transcribe it. Additionally, because the edited content remains in one place, you can avoid confusion about which is the most recent and can refine the same results together with your team.

screens.outro: Now that we have established a baseline, let's apply it to two requests.

screens.title: Explanatory example: web page design and report
screens.lead: The instructor demonstrates the process of determining the output units for two requests. Select the next arrow to follow your decision.

steps.title: Read two requests
steps.body: There are two requests. The first is a draft of the event introduction webpage, and the second is a quarterly report. Both requests initially start in chat, but the output has different uses. Units of output are determined by usage, not by name. Let's take a step-by-step look at why we don't handle both requests with the same tool.

steps.title: Step 1: Decide who will watch and where
steps.body: You should visually select a web page design and review it with your team. These results need to be visible and shareable right on the screen, so Artifact is a good fit. The quarterly report must be delivered to superiors as a file, so it must be in Word or PDF format.

steps.title: Step 2: See how many times to fix it
steps.body: When drafting a web page, text, color, and placement are modified several times. If you're going to edit it repeatedly, it's better to leave it as a deliverable and tell Claude to fix it or edit it yourself. If you copy and paste chat answers every time, the more edits you make, the more confused you become about which one is the most recent.

steps.title: Step 3: See if you need a file type
steps.body: Quarterly reports must be submitted as a Word document or PDF with tables and charts. In this case, create a Word or PDF file and download it. If you need to do numerical calculations, you can even create Excel to make the formulas work for you. If the artifact is in the form of a document, it can be exported to Word, PDF, Markdown, or Google Docs using Export.

steps.title: Step 4: Check the settings you need
steps.body: Both features require code execution and file creation to be turned on. Free, Pro, and Max follow the settings, and Team and Enterprise follow the organization settings set by the owner. If you don't see the feature, first make sure this toggle is turned off.

steps.title: Step 5: When an error occurs
steps.body: If you encounter an error in Artifact, click the Try fixing with Claude button near the error message. The error is copied into a new message and sent to Claude, who will attempt to diagnose the cause and fix it. It does not guarantee success and there may be errors that require further confirmation. If this error repeats, you can request the desired result again more specifically, or edit the previous message and create a separate version with a different direction. The separate versions you create allow you to explore different directions without losing your previous work.

steps.title: Conclusion
steps.body: The unit of the result is determined by its use. Explanations to be viewed once and passed through are created as conversations, drafts to be repeatedly revised and shared are created as Artifacts, and reports to be submitted in file format are created as files.

screens.outro: Now that we know how to determine the output unit, let's summarize the lesson.

screens.title: Summary: The longer you use it, the more output you get.
screens.lead: Let's summarize what we've seen so far. Read this while thinking about what output you need to produce.

paragraphs: Artifacts are artifacts that open next to a conversation to edit and share. These are artifacts you can show off to others, such as documents, slides, designs, dashboards, and small interactive tools, and you can find them again in the Artifacts tab. Results starting from a template can be opened and edited directly in the form of Docs, Slides, Design, etc.

File creation runs the code to create and download Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and PDF. Both features require code execution and file creation to be turned on, and for Team and Enterprise, the settings are based on the owner's settings.

The longer the result is used, the more important the format is, and the more it needs to be shared, the more it is created as a result. On the other hand, a conversation is enough to give an answer that you can only look at once.
There are three judgment orders: Decide who will see the results and where, see how many revisions will be made, and determine what file format is needed.

It is not difficult to judge if you apply the previous example of creating a web page draft as an Artifact because it needs to be repeatedly revised and shared, and a quarterly report as a file creation because it requires a file for submission, to this order. Ultimately, the unit of output is determined by its use, not its name.

callout.label: Note
callout.text: Artifacts are results that you can edit and come back to and share. It's not just about embellishing chat responses.

glossary.def: It's a result you can show to others that opens next to the conversation and allows you to edit and share it yourself.
This function allows you to run code to create and download Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and PDF files.
It is a cloud execution environment that enables file creation and artifacts.
Like Docs, Slides, and Design, this is the format you choose when starting the output.
It is a result that is re-opened, modified, and shared, and is used longer than a conversation.

misconceptions.myth: Artifacts are pretty decorations for chat responses.
misconceptions.fact: Artifacts are output that you can edit directly next to a conversation and then return to share or export. It is not just a simple decoration, but the unit of result is different.

misconceptions.myth: File creation is turned on equally in all plans.
misconceptions.fact: Free, Pro, and Max are turned on in the settings, and Team and Enterprise are set by the owner in the organization settings. Network access is also turned off by default in Team and Enterprise.

misconceptions.myth: Output is always better than a conversational answer.
misconceptions.fact: A conversation is enough for a quick explanation or quick confirmation. The output is appropriate when it is something that will be used for a long time, shared, or modified repeatedly.

closing.lead: Summarizes the key points of this class.
points: Conversations are something you see once and pass by, while output is something you use for a long time.
Artifacts are edited and shared alongside conversations.
File Creation creates Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and PDF.
The longer the result is used, the more it is made into an output.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for self-thinking purposes only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: Among the results I create, what do I need to reopen, edit, or show to others?

checks.q: You need to look at the event introduction webpage draft, revise it several times, and share it with others. Which one is best?
options: I receive it as a chat reply and copy it every time.
A quick look and a passing conversation response is enough.
Create an artifact and edit and share it next to the conversation.
The results are first downloaded as a Word file only.
checks.explain: Results that are to be repeatedly modified and shared are outputs. The longer it is used and the more important the format, the more suitable the output.

wrong.0: The advantage of the output is that it reduces the effort of copying and moving.
wrong.1: The conversation answer fits the explanation that you just glance at and pass by.
wrong.3: For drafts that are viewed, modified, and shared, it is better to use output rather than a file.

checks.intro: Choose the type of result you want to edit and share over and over again.
checks.correctFeedback: That's right. Artifact is ideal for results that you want to see with your own eyes, edit several times, and share.
checks.incorrectFeedback: Chat replies must be copied and moved each time, and the file format is determined according to the last need. Rewatch based on number of edits and need to share.

checks.q: Correctly establish the order of judgment that determines the form of the result
items: Decide who sees the results and where
Let's see how many times I fix it.
See if the file format is needed
checks.explain: Choose the viewer and location, see the number of modifications, and finally check whether the file format is needed.
checks.intro: Arrange the order of decisions that determine the shape of the outcome.
checks.correctFeedback: The order is correct. You've narrowed it down to who will see it where, how many times it will be modified, and whether the file format is needed.
checks.incorrectFeedback: The order is out of order. Decide on the file format last, decide who and where to view it first, and look at the number of modifications.
